question: Which disclosure-policy configurations lie on the Pareto frontier across reconstruction risk, legitimate utility, availability, and accounting cost?
raw_idea: Compare security controls without pretending that maximum denial is a useful security solution.
initial_claim: Different policies occupy different security-utility trade-off regions.
narrowed_claim: A unified paired benchmark can identify non-dominated and robustly dominated tested configurations without hiding task weights in one score.
hypothesis: Frontier membership will depend on task mix and deadline, while some configurations remain dominated across most declared profiles.
strongest_objections: Pareto results depend on selected metrics and configurations.
Task weights may encode the desired conclusion.
Toy latency and storage costs may be meaningless.
A1–A3 mechanisms may not be comparable in one harness.

criteria: Frontier membership is unstable across seeds and small specification changes.
One metric silently controls every result.

success_criteria: Every policy uses identical paired trials.
Stable and weight-sensitive conclusions are separated.
Deadline and task-profile frontiers are reported independently.

experiment.plan: Run a unified parameter grid for baseline, rate, quota, coverage, hybrid, and adaptive policies across six workloads and four deadline conditions.

claim_audit: No policy family is declared dominated from one configuration.
A1–A3 published summaries are not mixed without unified reruns.

next_questions: When does rate limiting enter the frontier?
Which task profiles make adaptive disclosure non-dominated?
